subject: SDLC custody mapping + ephemeral access log request (SIG intake)
messages:
From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@quantifyassess.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Peter Sykes <peter.sykes@regbank.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: SDLC custody mapping + ephemeral access log request (SIG intake)

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking our SIG intake. As part of the developer & deployment controls section we need: 1) a custody mapping that shows which teams/individuals have access to signing keys, keystore/HSM, and who is authorized to approve production merges; and 2) a sample ephemeral access log covering a recent 7-day window that demonstrates rotation/short-lived credential issuance and revocation events.

For the custody mapping please include columns: resource (keystore/KMS/service account), owner (team/person), approval authority (role), last rotation date, and current delegated stewards. For the access log sample we mostly need timestamp, subject (principal), action (issue/revoke/use), resource referenced, and correlation id. A redacted sample is fine; we just want to validate controls and timelines.

Can you get this to us by EOD PT Tuesday (2027-04-06)? If a drive link is easier, that works. Also flag any known exceptions or pending change requests that might affect the window.

Best,
Emily
Emily Zhang
Senior Assessor, Quantify Assess
emily.zhang@quantifyassess.com

--
Attachment: SIG-intake-checklist.pdf (referenced)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@quantifyassess.com>
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Sun, 4 Apr 2027 17:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDLC custody mapping + ephemeral access log request (SIG intake)

Emily —

Thanks for the clear ask. We'll assemble a redacted custody matrix and a 7-day ephemeral access sample. A couple quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly:

- Do you want the matrix at the individual IAM principal level, or is team-level ownership acceptable for keystore entries (we can provide both but team-level reduces PII exposure)?
- For the ephemeral access log, should we include internal admin actions (token minting by operators) or only programmatic issuance tied to CI/CD runs?

Irene, Jordan, Soojin — can you pick this up? Jordan, if you can export a 7-day sample from the ephemeral token service and redact principal IDs that would be ideal. Irene, please prepare the custody mapping CSV and include the rotation dates and ticket references for the last rotation. Soojin, please scan our change-management ticket list for any pending exceptions covering the sample window and add a short note.

We'll plan to upload to a shared drive and send a download link. If Quantify needs a time-limited viewer link or DocuSign acknowledgement for delivery, let me know.

Thanks —
Karthik
Sr. Manager, Platform Security
Redwood Inference

> On Apr 4, 2027, at 16:12, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@quantifyassess.com> wrote:
> > [original request]

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@quantifyassess.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwoodinference.com>, Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDLC custody mapping + ephemeral access log request (SIG intake)

Emily / team —

Attached are the artifacts we discussed: custody-mapping-2027-04-05.csv and ephemeral-access-sample-7days.log. I included a short PDF (change-ownership-notes-20270405.pdf) that summarizes relevant change requests and approvals during the sample window.

Notes on redaction and scope:
- The custody CSV is provided at the team + role granularity; where reviewers require individual principal names we can provide a separate sensitive export under NDA. Columns: resource, owner_team, steward_role, approval_authority, last_rotation_ticket, last_rotation_date.
- The access log is a 7-day slice (2027-03-28 to 2027-04-03). We redacted principal IDs to the form svc-<team>-xxxx and kept correlation_id for traceability. The sample includes both CI-token issuance events and operator-issued admin tokens; we annotated event_type in the log.
- We confirm keystore material is stored in a customer-managed KMS (CloudKMS) with HSM-backed keys; rotation events are recorded in ticket references listed in the CSV.

If you need any additional columns or a longer window (e.g., 30 days), let us know and we can produce that. For SOC2 reviewers that want deterministic provenance we can also export the PR merge history and the deploy run IDs that correlate to token issuance events.

Drive link (viewer-only, expires 2027-05-05): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1QfExampleDriveId

--
Irene Choi
Manager, Application Security
Redwood Inference

Attachments: custody-mapping-2027-04-05.csv, ephemeral-access-sample-7days.log, change-ownership-notes-20270405.pdf

From: Emily Zhang <emily.zhang@quantifyassess.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Peter Sykes <peter.sykes@regbank.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 6 Apr 2027 09:34:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SDLC custody mapping + ephemeral access log request (SIG intake)

Irene / Karthik —

Received, thank you. The CSV and sample log look good for our initial review. One small ask: can you add a single additional column to the custody CSV called "last_reviewed_by" with the name (or team role) who validated the mapping last quarter? That helps the SIG assessor confirm periodic review without needing individual PII.

If you can upload a brief one-paragraph attestation (signed by a security manager) confirming that the sample log covers production-scope token issuance and that redaction did not remove correlation ids, that would be ideal. Otherwise we're happy to proceed with what you sent and flag a follow-up if needed.

Thanks again — will loop back after the quick pass.

Best,
Emily
Senior Assessor, Quantify Assess
